teams.heading: Warren Gatland among 31 applicants to become new Fiji head coach
teams.body: Former Wales boss Warren Gatland has emerged as a surprise candidate to lead Fiji, following reports that 31 coaches have applied to succeed Mick Byrne. The recruitment process enters its final stage today, coinciding with the official start date listed in the original job advertisement. While interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula currently oversees the squad, the Fiji Rugby Union is expected to name a permanent appointment shortly to lead the Flying Fijians against France, Ireland and Italy next month.

lead.why: It highlights the shock application of Warren Gatland and the scale of the 31-man shortlist, providing a fresh angle from the coaching search news reported earlier today.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick retains RFU backing despite persistent scrutiny over England’s tactical identity
teams.body: Steve Borthwick retains the long-term backing of the RFU to lead England into next year’s World Cup, despite ongoing scrutiny regarding the team’s tactical direction. While the head coach is praised for a 'Spock-like approach' to analysis, critics suggest his tenure is marked by contradictions between data-led pragmatism and the team's best performances when playing with more freedom. Following a review-heavy period and a historic loss to Italy, Borthwick must now reconcile his reputation for 'thinking like a machine' with the need for a settled, cohesive gameplan.

teams.heading: Peter O’Mahony details his disappointment over Rassie Erasmus’s Munster departure
teams.body: Former captain Peter O’Mahony has revealed the impact of Rassie Erasmus’s departure from Munster, admitting the exit left him feeling hurt at the time. Speaking on the Indo Sport podcast, the veteran forward explained that he had fully committed to the director of rugby’s game plan and believed the team was on the cusp of significant progress. While acknowledging that it was a ruthless business decision, O’Mahony noted he now understands the professional motivation behind the move back to South Africa.

teams.heading: Hector Patterson monitors options as Bath circle Edinburgh scrum-half prospect
teams.body: Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson is attracting interest from English and French clubs, with Bath reportedly tracking the 21-year-old. Patterson, the son of former Scotland international Derrick, remains under contract at Edinburgh but his eligibility for England via a grandparent presents an intriguing subplot. Having represented Scotland through the age-grade system, including a win at the 2024 World Rugby U20 Trophy, his international future remains open until he is senior-capped. His next move is being closely watched ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

teams.heading: Jeremy Williams backs resurgent Wallabies to challenge for 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Wallabies lock Jeremy Williams has backed Australia to challenge for the Webb Ellis Cup at next year’s home World Cup, as the team continues to build momentum under coach Les Kiss. Currently ranked sixth in the world, the side has remained unbeaten under Kiss, whose tenure has seen a first series win in Argentina and a gritty victory against South Africa. "The team we’ve got, the players, coaching staff, and the drive, the care that we have for each other," Williams said.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie confirms All Blacks remain committed to aerial game tactics
teams.body: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has confirmed the side will not abandon their high-ball strategy, despite difficulties encountered against the Springboks during the recent Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series. New Zealand has adopted a tactic of sprinting back to catch kicks rather than running onto the ball. Rennie acknowledged the team struggled aerially against South Africa but maintained they are moving in the right direction, noting that the players have embraced the high-tempo style he is instilling since taking charge.

teams.heading: Jake White emerges as favourite for Fiji head coach role
teams.body: Former Springboks head coach Jake White has reportedly emerged as the leading candidate to take charge of Fiji ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. While Fiji’s national union has received 31 applications for the vacancy, sources indicate White is currently the favourite to be appointed. If successful, it would mark White’s first international head coaching role since leading South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007. The appointment is expected to be confirmed in the coming days.
